title: Checkpoint: Values and Variables
intro: Test your understanding of variables, numbers, strings, f-strings, input, and reading errors.

questions.question: What does this code print?
questions.explanation: y = x makes y point to the value 5. Giving x a new value later does not change y.

questions.question: What does this code print?
questions.explanation: // gives the whole part of the division (3) and % gives the remainder (1).

questions.question: What does this code print?
questions.explanation: / always gives a float, even when the division is exact. // gives an int when both sides are ints.

questions.question: What does this code print?
questions.explanation: Index -1 is the last character, and a slice stops before the stop index, so [0:4] gives the first 4 characters.

questions.question: What does this code print?
questions.explanation: String methods return a new string; they never change the original. Save the result: city = city.capitalize().

questions.question: The user types 20. What does this code print?
questions.explanation: input() always returns a string, and a string times 2 repeats it. Convert first with int(input(...)).

questions.question: What happens when you run this code?
questions.explanation: Python will not join a string and an int automatically. Use str(total) or an f-string.

questions.question: What happens when you run this code?
questions.explanation: int() cannot read text that contains a decimal point. Use float() when the value can have decimals.

questions.question: A long traceback appears on your screen. Where should you look first?
options: The first line, Traceback (most recent call last):
The last line, which names the error and describes it
Nowhere; just change code until it works
questions.explanation: The useful information is at the bottom: the error type and message. The lines above show where it happened.
